# lds_journal - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lds-journal/0.8.0/lds_journal/

## Expand description

Journal module for local-develop-server (lds).

[§](https://docs.rs#architecture)Architecture

Thin wrapper around `journal-mcp-rmcp::JournalMcpServer`. Delegates
`list_tools` / `call_tool` / `list_resources` / `read_resource` to the
upstream MCP server. Unlike `lds-outline`, no name-prefix rewriting is
needed — journal-mcp’s 17 tools are already namespaced with the
`journal_` prefix in-crate (`journal_open_chapter`,
`journal_append_section`, …), so the wrapper just detects that prefix
on incoming tool calls and forwards verbatim.

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

- Session root is passed at construction (typically
`session.root().to_path_buf()`from`crates/lds/src/main.rs`); the module itself is location-agnostic.
- File projection (rendering the journal to a Markdown file) is
opt-in: the caller passes `Some(path)`in`RunConfig::file_projection`to attach it at startup. Runtime attach/detach continues to work through the`journal_projection_*`MCP tools.
- Resource URIs (`journal-mcp://*`if any) are forwarded verbatim through the ServerHandler.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use module::`- [JournalModule](https://docs.rs/module/struct.JournalModule.html);
- `pub use`- [journal_mcp_rmcp](https://docs.rs/journal-mcp-rmcp/0.5.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/journal_mcp_rmcp/index.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [module](https://docs.rs/module/index.html)
- `JournalModule`- `JournalMcpServer`.

# lds_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lds-core/0.8.0/lds_core/

## Expand description

Core utilities shared across all lds modules.

Session lifecycle (`Session`, `LdsState`, `SessionConfig`, `SessionError`,
`CoreError`) lives in the sibling `lds-session` crate and is re-exported
here for backward compatibility — existing `use lds_core::Session;` etc.
continues to work unchanged.

This crate retains cross-cutting helpers that do not belong to the
session contract: binary probing (`find_in_path`, `check_binaries`,
`BinaryStatus`), output truncation (`truncate_output`), config file
handling (`config` module), and the in-memory log ring (`log_store`).

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Binary](https://docs.rs/struct.BinaryStatus.html)- Status
- Availability status for an external binary.
- [Doctor](https://docs.rs/struct.DoctorCheck.html)- Check
- [Doctor](https://docs.rs/struct.DoctorReport.html)- Report
- [LdsState](https://docs.rs/struct.LdsState.html)
- Top-level mutable state for the MCP server.
- [Session](https://docs.rs/struct.Session.html)
- Immutable session state created by `session_start`/`session_create`.
- [Session](https://docs.rs/struct.SessionConfig.html)- Config
- Configuration passed to `Session::new`
- [Session](https://docs.rs/struct.SessionEntry.html)- Entry
- Snapshot of a single session entry, returned by ledger introspection APIs.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Check](https://docs.rs/enum.CheckStatus.html)- Status
- Per-check verdict returned by `LdsState::doctor`
- [Core](https://docs.rs/enum.CoreError.html)- Error
- Errors that can occur during session construction or access.
- [Session](https://docs.rs/enum.SessionError.html)- Error
- Errors that can occur during a `Session`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [check_](https://docs.rs/fn.check_binaries.html)- binaries
- Check a set of external binaries and return their availability.
- [find_](https://docs.rs/fn.find_in_path.html)- in_ - path
- Check whether an executable is reachable via `PATH`.
- [truncate_](https://docs.rs/fn.truncate_output.html)- output
- Truncate byte output to `max`bytes, splitting into head + tail halves.

# ecdsa - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ecdsa/0.17.0/ecdsa/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#rustcrypto-ecdsa)[RustCrypto](https://github.com/RustCrypto): ECDSA

[Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elliptic_Curve_Digital_Signature_Algorithm) as specified in
[FIPS 186-4](https://csrc.nist.gov/publications/detail/fips/186/4/final) (Digital Signature Standard).

[§](https://docs.rs#about)About

This crate provides generic ECDSA support which can be used in the following ways:

- Generic implementation of ECDSA usable with the following crates:
- Other crates which provide their own complete implementations of ECDSA can
also leverage the types from this crate to export ECDSA functionality in a
generic, interoperable way by leveraging `ecdsa::Signature``signature::Signer``signature::Verifier`

[§](https://docs.rs#-security-warning)⚠️ Security Warning

The ECDSA implementation contained in this crate has never been independently audited for security!

This crate contains a generic implementation of ECDSA which must be instantiated using a separate crate providing a concrete implementation of arithmetic for a particular curve. It’s possible timing variability can exist in concrete curve implementations, and thus this crate’s security can only be properly assessed for a specific elliptic curve.

USE AT YOUR OWN RISK!

[§](https://docs.rs#license)License

All crates licensed under either of

at your option.

[§](https://docs.rs#contribution)Contribution

Unless you explicitly state otherwise, any contribution intentionally submitted for inclusion in the work by you, as defined in the Apache-2.0 license, shall be dual licensed as above, without any additional terms or conditions.

[§](https://docs.rs#serde-support)`serde` support

When the `serde` feature of this crate is enabled, `Serialize` and `Deserialize` impls are
provided for the [ Signature](https://docs.rs/struct.Signature.html) and

[types.](https://docs.rs/struct.VerifyingKey.html)

`VerifyingKey`Please see type-specific documentation for more information.

[§](https://docs.rs#interop)Interop

Any crates which provide an implementation of ECDSA for a particular elliptic curve can leverage
the types from this crate, along with the [ k256](https://docs.rs/k256),

[, and/or](https://docs.rs/p256)

`p256`[crates to expose ECDSA functionality in a generic, interoperable way by leveraging the](https://docs.rs/p384)

`p384`[type with in conjunction with the](https://docs.rs/struct.Signature.html)

`Signature`[and](https://docs.rs/signature/latest/signature/trait.Signer.html)

`signature::Signer`[traits.](https://docs.rs/signature/latest/signature/trait.Verifier.html)

`signature::Verifier`For example, the [ ring-compat](https://docs.rs/ring-compat) crate implements the

[and](https://docs.rs/signature/latest/signature/trait.Signer.html)

`signature::Signer`[traits in conjunction with the](https://docs.rs/signature/latest/signature/trait.Verifier.html)

`signature::Verifier`[and](https://docs.rs/p256/latest/p256/ecdsa/type.Signature.html)

`p256::ecdsa::Signature`[types to wrap the ECDSA implementations from](https://docs.rs/p384/latest/p384/ecdsa/type.Signature.html)

`p384::ecdsa::Signature`[in a generic, interoperable API.](https://docs.rs/ring)

*ring*## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

# lds_recipe - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lds-recipe/0.8.0/lds_recipe/

## Expand description

Justfile recipe execution with hierarchical resolve chain.

Discovers justfiles at two levels — Global (`~/.config/lds/`) and
Project (`{root}/`) — merges their recipes (project wins on name
collision), and tags each recipe with [ ResolveInfo](https://docs.rs/struct.ResolveInfo.html) so callers
know which justfile it came from. Adding a level (e.g. Worktree)
is one enum variant + one path probe.

Execution applies [ Session](https://docs.rs/lds-session/0.8.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lds_session/struct.Session.html) timeout and output truncation, and
injects

`content` args as `TASK_MCP_CONTENT_{KEY}` environment
variables for the recipe process.## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [list_](https://docs.rs/fn.list_global_plugins.html)- global_ - plugins
- Scan global plugin recipes from all global dirs, in precedence order.

# lds_gh - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lds-gh/0.8.0/lds_gh/

## Expand description

GitHub CLI wrapper module for local-develop-server (lds).

Provides [ GhModule](https://docs.rs/struct.GhModule.html) — a read-only wrapper around the

`gh` CLI subprocess.
All write operations (`gh pr create`, `gh issue create`, `gh release create`,
`gh pr merge`) are intentionally absent: they are structurally excluded from
the MCP surface per the cross-cutting AI safety rule (write tool AI-禁止).[§](https://docs.rs#security-design)Security design

Every subprocess call goes through [`gh_cmd`], which:

- Calls [`gh_auth_check`] first — fails fast if not authenticated.
- Uses `Command::new("gh").args(args)`(shell=false, arg-by-arg). No string concatenation or`sh -c`is used anywhere in this crate.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [GhModule](https://docs.rs/struct.GhModule.html)
- GitHub CLI subprocess wrapper with session context.

# fsmon - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fsmon/0.5.1/fsmon/

## Expand description

fsmon - 轻量级高性能文件系统监控工具

[§](https://docs.rs#%E6%A6%82%E8%BF%B0)概述

fsmon 是一个基于 fanotify 的 Linux 文件系统监控工具，提供以下功能：

- **实时监控**：监控文件系统的创建、修改、删除、移动等事件
- **事件过滤**：支持按路径、事件类型、文件大小等进行过滤
- **日志记录**：将事件记录到 JSONL 格式的日志文件中
- **历史查询**：支持查询历史事件记录
- **守护进程**：支持作为 systemd 服务运行

[§](https://docs.rs#%E4%BD%BF%E7%94%A8%E7%A4%BA%E4%BE%8B)使用示例

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
let config = MonitorConfig {
    paths_and_options: vec![(PathBuf::from("/home/user"), PathOptions::default())],
    log_dir: Some(PathBuf::from("/var/log/fsmon")),
    debug: true,
    ..Default::default()
};
// let monitor = Monitor::new(config)?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#%E6%A8%A1%E5%9D%97%E7%BB%93%E6%9E%84)模块结构

- `common`

[§](https://docs.rs#%E5%B9%B3%E5%8F%B0%E6%94%AF%E6%8C%81)平台支持

目前仅支持 Linux 系统（需要 fanotify 支持）。

# tatara_net - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tatara-net/0.2.116/tatara_net/

## Expand description

tatara-net: Cross-platform networking plane for the tatara cluster fabric.

The complete sandwich:

```
┌─ WASI (wasmtime) ──── Portable, sandboxed workloads ─────────┐
├─ Tatara Runtime ───── Convergence, scheduling, Raft ─────────┤
├─ eBPF (aya) ────────── Kernel hooks, pure Rust ──────────────┤
├─ WireGuard (mamorigami) ─ Encrypted mesh fabric ─────────────┤
└─ Hardware ──────────── Abstracted away ──────────────────────┘
```
On Linux: eBPF programs (XDP/TC/cgroup) for kernel-level networking. On macOS: userspace networking via tun-rs + smoltcp + hanabi proxy. Everywhere: WireGuard mesh via mamorigami for encrypted inter-node traffic.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use config::`- [NetConfig](https://docs.rs/config/struct.NetConfig.html);
- `pub use traits::`- [NetworkPlane](https://docs.rs/traits/trait.NetworkPlane.html);
- `pub use`- [types](https://docs.rs/types/index.html)::*;

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- Networking plane configuration.
- [convergence](https://docs.rs/convergence/index.html)
- Module stub — implementation in later phases.
- [mesh](https://docs.rs/mesh/index.html)
- Module stub — implementation in later phases.
- [observability](https://docs.rs/observability/index.html)
- Module stub — implementation in later phases.
- [platform](https://docs.rs/platform/index.html)
- Module stub — implementation in later phases.
- [policy](https://docs.rs/policy/index.html)
- Module stub — implementation in later phases.

- Module stub — implementation in later phases.

# arora-buffers 0.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/arora-buffers/0.1.0

Please check the

[build logs](https://docs.rs/crate/arora-buffers/0.1.0/builds)for more information.

See

[Builds](https://docs.rs/about/builds)for ideas on how to fix a failed build, or

[Metadata](https://docs.rs/about/metadata)for how to configure docs.rs builds.

If you believe this is docs.rs' fault,

[open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose).

# Arora Buffers

The buffers are used for exchanges across the module boundaries.
It can represent all the data structures into an `[u8]`.
It starts with 4 bytes (32 bits) representing the size of the whole buffer.
It is limited to 32 bits to match WASM's current implementation.

Please refer to the [read](https://docs.rs/src/read.rs) and [write](https://docs.rs/src/write.rs) functions
for the details of the buffer format.

This library provides functions to [serialize and deserialize buffers
from generic  Values](https://docs.rs/src/serde_uuid.rs)),
as defined in the

`arora-types`This library also provides [an exported function to allocate or free a buffer](https://docs.rs/src/alloc.rs).

# arora_behavior - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/arora-behavior/0.1.0/arora_behavior/

## Expand description

The behavior abstraction: anything the Arora runtime can tick.

A [ Behavior](https://docs.rs/trait.Behavior.html) is the runtime’s “what to do each step”. The behavior tree is
one (

`arora-behavior-tree`’s `TreeBehavior`); a Vizij node graph is another.
The runtime accepts any of them interchangeably — it just swaps the
interpreter.Each tick a behavior gets a [ BehaviorContext](https://docs.rs/struct.BehaviorContext.html): the shared

[(read inputs, write intent / outputs), a](https://docs.rs/arora-types/1.5.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/arora_types/data/store/trait.DataStore.html)

`DataStore`[(so module-calling behaviors like the behavior tree can reach the engine), and the frame delta. A behavior uses whichever it needs — a graph reads/writes the store; the tree drives the caller.](https://docs.rs/arora-types/1.5.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/arora_types/call/trait.CallBridge.html)

`CallBridge`## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Behavior](https://docs.rs/struct.BehaviorContext.html)- Context
- What a `Behavior``tick`
- [Behavior](https://docs.rs/struct.BehaviorError.html)- Error
- A behavior failed to tick.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Behavior](https://docs.rs/enum.BehaviorStatus.html)- Status
- Whether a behavior wants to be ticked again.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Behavior](https://docs.rs/trait.Behavior.html)
- Something the Arora runtime ticks once per step.

# lds_git - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/lds-git/0.8.0/lds_git/

## Expand description

Git operations backed by [ git2](https://docs.rs/git2/0.20.4/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/git2/index.html), with session-scoped write safety.

Every public method returns a typed [ output](https://docs.rs/output/index.html) struct wrapped in

[. The lds MCP layer serialises these structs with](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0.102/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/anyhow/type.Result.html)

`anyhow::Result``serde_json::to_string_pretty` so callers receive a stable JSON shape and
can access fields directly instead of parsing free-form text.Read operations (status, log, diff, worktree_list, remote inspection) are
always available. Write operations (commit, merge, worktree add/remove,
branch delete, reset) require the target path / branch to have been
created — or formally adopted via [ GitModule::session_release](https://docs.rs/struct.GitModule.html#method.session_release) — by the
current session.

# tatara_mcp - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tatara-mcp/0.2.116/tatara_mcp/

## Expand description

Tatara MCP server — AI-assisted convergence computing.

Provides 30 MCP tools organized in 5 categories for AI agents to observe, analyze, influence, verify, and report on convergence state.

This is the Intelligence dimension (6th classification axis) of the convergence computing model. AI interacts with the convergence ether through structured, typed, purpose-built tools.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- MCP tool categories — every tool belongs to exactly one.

---

# wasm-bindgen 0.2.126 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wasm-bindgen/0.2.126

Built with 🦀🕸 by The Rust and WebAssembly Working Group

## Install `wasm-bindgen-cli`

You can install it using `cargo install`:

```
cargo install wasm-bindgen-cli
```
Or, you can download it from the
[release page](https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen/releases).

If you have [ cargo-binstall](https://crates.io/crates/cargo-binstall) installed,
then you can install the pre-built artifacts by running:

```
cargo binstall wasm-bindgen-cli
```
## Example

Import JavaScript things into Rust and export Rust things to JavaScript.

```
use *;
// Import the `window.alert` function from the Web.
extern "C"
// Export a `greet` function from Rust to JavaScript, that alerts a
// hello message.
```
Use exported Rust things from JavaScript with ECMAScript modules!

```
import  from "./hello_world";
;
```
## Features

-
**Lightweight.**Only pay for what you use.`wasm-bindgen`only generates bindings and glue for the JavaScript imports you actually use and Rust functionality that you export. For example, importing and using the`document.querySelector`method doesn't cause`Node.prototype.appendChild`or`window.alert`to be included in the bindings as well.
-
**ECMAScript modules.**Just import WebAssembly modules the same way you would import JavaScript modules. Future compatible with[WebAssembly modules and ECMAScript modules integration](https://github.com/WebAssembly/esm-integration).
-
**Designed with the**Eventually, there won't be any JavaScript shims between Rust-generated wasm functions and native DOM methods. Because the Wasm functions are statically type checked, some of those native methods' dynamic type checks should become unnecessary, promising to unlock even-faster-than-JavaScript DOM access.["Web IDL bindings" proposal](https://github.com/WebAssembly/proposals/issues/8)in mind.

## Guide

## API Docs

## MSRV Policy

- Libraries that are released on [crates.io](https://crates.io)have a MSRV of v1.77.
- CLI tools and their corresponding support libraries have a MSRV of v1.86.

The project aims to maintain a 2-year MSRV policy for libraries (meaning we support Rust versions released within the last 2 years), but with a shorter MSRV policy for the CLI. Changes to the MSRV may be made in patch versions, and will be logged in the CHANGELOG and MSRV history below.

### MSRV History

| Version | Library MSRV | CLI MSRV | Date |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.2.118 | 1.77 | 1.86 | 2026-04-10 |
| 0.2.106 | 1.71 | 1.82 | 2025-11-27 |
| 0.2.103 | 1.57 | 1.82 | 2025-09-17 |
| 0.2.93 | 1.57 | 1.76 | 2024-08-13 |

# wasm_bindgen - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/wasm-bindgen/0.2.126/target-redirect/wasm_bindgen/

## Expand description

Runtime support for the `wasm-bindgen` tool

This crate contains the runtime support necessary for `wasm-bindgen` the
attribute and tool. Crates pull in the `#[wasm_bindgen]` attribute through
this crate and this crate also provides JS bindings through the `JsValue`
interface.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

[§](https://docs.rs#enable-interning)`enable-interning`

Enables the internal cache for [`wasm_bindgen::intern`].

This feature currently enables the `std` feature, meaning that it is not
compatible with `no_std` environments.

[§](https://docs.rs#std-default)`std` (default)

Enabling this feature will make the crate depend on the Rust standard library.

Disable this feature to use this crate in `no_std` environments.

[§](https://docs.rs#strict-macro)`strict-macro`

All warnings the `#[wasm_bindgen]` macro emits are turned into hard errors.
This mainly affects unused attribute options.

[§](https://docs.rs#deprecated-features)Deprecated features

[§](https://docs.rs#serde-serialize)`serde-serialize`

**Deprecated:** Use the [ serde-wasm-bindgen](https://docs.rs/serde-wasm-bindgen/latest/serde_wasm_bindgen/) crate instead.

Enables the `JsValue::from_serde` and `JsValue::into_serde` methods for
serializing and deserializing Rust types to and from JavaScript.

[§](https://docs.rs#spans)`spans`

**Deprecated:** This feature became a no-op in wasm-bindgen v0.2.20 (Sep 7, 2018).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::convert::`- [IntoJsGeneric](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.IntoJsGeneric.html);
- `pub use crate::convert::`- [JsGeneric](https://docs.rs/convert/trait.JsGeneric.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [closure](https://docs.rs/closure/index.html)
- Support for closures in `wasm-bindgen`
- [convert](https://docs.rs/convert/index.html)
- ⚠️ Unstable
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- A module which is typically glob imported.
- [sys](https://docs.rs/sys/index.html)
- JavaScript system types that are re-exported by `js-sys`.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [link_to](https://docs.rs/macro.link_to.html)
- This macro takes a JS module as input and returns a URL that can be used to access it at runtime.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Clamped](https://docs.rs/struct.Clamped.html)
- A wrapper type around slices and vectors for binding the `Uint8ClampedArray`array in JS.
- [JsError](https://docs.rs/struct.JsError.html)
- Convenience type for use on exported `fn() -> Result<T, JsError>`functions, where you wish to throw a JavaScript`Error`object.
- [JsStatic](https://docs.rs/struct.JsStatic.html)- Deprecated
- Wrapper type for imported statics.
- [JsThread](https://docs.rs/struct.JsThreadLocal.html)- Local
- Wrapper type for imported statics.
- [JsValue](https://docs.rs/struct.JsValue.html)
- Representation of an object owned by JS.
- [Parent](https://docs.rs/struct.Parent.html)
- Storage wrapper for the auto-injected `parent`field on a struct that declares`#[wasm_bindgen(extends = Parent)]`.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Erasable](https://docs.rs/trait.ErasableGeneric.html)- Generic
- Private marker trait for erasable generics - types with this trait have the same repr for all generic param values, and can therefore be transmuted on the singular Repr type representation on ABI boundaries.
- [JsCast](https://docs.rs/trait.JsCast.html)
- A trait for dynamic checked and unchecked casting between JS types.
- [Unwrap](https://docs.rs/trait.UnwrapThrowExt.html)- Throw - Ext
- An extension trait for `Option<T>`and`Result<T, E>`for unwrapping the`T`value, or throwing a JS error if it is not available.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [exports](https://docs.rs/fn.exports.html)
- Returns a handle to this Wasm instance’s `WebAssembly.Instance.prototype.exports`
- [externref_](https://docs.rs/fn.externref_heap_live_count.html)- heap_ - live_ - count
- Get the count of live `externref`s /`JsValue`s in`wasm-bindgen`’s heap.
- [function_](https://docs.rs/fn.function_table.html)- table
- Returns a handle to this Wasm instance’s `WebAssembly.Table`which is the indirect function table used by Rust
- [instance](https://docs.rs/fn.instance.html)
- Returns a handle to this Wasm instance’s `WebAssembly.Instance`. This is only available when the final Wasm app is built with`--target no-modules`,`--target web`,`--target deno`or`--target nodejs`. It is unavailable for`--target bundler`.
- [intern](https://docs.rs/fn.intern.html)
- Interns Rust strings so that it’s much faster to send them to JS.
- [memory](https://docs.rs/fn.memory.html)
- Returns a handle to this Wasm instance’s `WebAssembly.Memory`
- [module](https://docs.rs/fn.module.html)
- Returns a handle to this Wasm instance’s `WebAssembly.Module`. This is only available when the final Wasm app is built with`--target no-modules`,`--target web`,`--target deno`or`--target nodejs`. It is unavailable for`--target bundler`.
- [throw_](https://docs.rs/fn.throw_str.html)- str
- Throws a JS exception.
- [throw_](https://docs.rs/fn.throw_val.html)- val
- Rethrow a JS exception
- [unintern](https://docs.rs/fn.unintern.html)
- Removes a Rust string from the intern cache.

[70](https://docs.rs#70)
[71](https://docs.rs#71)const _: () = {
[72](https://docs.rs#72)    /// Dummy empty function provided in order to detect linker-injected functions like `__wasm_call_ctors` and others that should be skipped by the wasm-bindgen interpreter.
[73](https://docs.rs#73)    ///
[74](https://docs.rs#74)    /// ## About `__wasm_call_ctors`
[75](https://docs.rs#75)    ///
[76](https://docs.rs#76)    /// There are several ways `__wasm_call_ctors` is introduced by the linker:
[77](https://docs.rs#77)    ///
[78](https://docs.rs#78)    /// * Using `#[link_section = ".init_array"]`;
[79](https://docs.rs#79)    /// * Linking with a C library that uses `__attribute__((constructor))`.
[80](https://docs.rs#80)    ///
[81](https://docs.rs#81)    /// The Wasm linker will insert a call to the `__wasm_call_ctors` function at the beginning of every
[82](https://docs.rs#82)    /// function that your module exports if it regards a module as having "command-style linkage".
[83](https://docs.rs#83)    /// Specifically, it regards a module as having "command-style linkage" if:
[84](https://docs.rs#84)    ///
[85](https://docs.rs#85)    /// * it is not relocatable;
[86](https://docs.rs#86)    /// * it is not a position-independent executable;
[87](https://docs.rs#87)    /// * and it does not call `__wasm_call_ctors`, directly or indirectly, from any
[88](https://docs.rs#88)    ///   exported function.
[89](https://docs.rs#89)    #[no_mangle]
[90](https://docs.rs#90)    pub extern "C" fn __wbindgen_skip_interpret_calls() {}
[91](https://docs.rs#91)};
[92](https://docs.rs#92)
[93](https://docs.rs#93)macro_rules! externs {
[94](https://docs.rs#94)    ($(#[$attr:meta])* extern "C" { $(fn $name:ident($($args:tt)*) -> $ret:ty;)* }) => (
[95](https://docs.rs#95)        #[cfg(all(target_family = "wasm", not(target_os = "wasi")))]
[96](https://docs.rs#96)        $(#[$attr])*
[97](https://docs.rs#97)        extern "C" {
[98](https://docs.rs#98)            $(fn $name($($args)*) -> $ret;)*
[99](https://docs.rs#99)        }
[100](https://docs.rs#100)
[101](https://docs.rs#101)        $(
[102](https://docs.rs#102)            #[cfg(not(all(target_family = "wasm", not(target_os = "wasi"))))]
[103](https://docs.rs#103)            #[allow(unused_variables)]
[104](https://docs.rs#104)            unsafe extern "C" fn $name($($args)*) -> $ret {
[105](https://docs.rs#105)                panic!("function not implemented on non-wasm32 targets")
[106](https://docs.rs#106)            }
[107](https://docs.rs#107)        )*
[108](https://docs.rs#108)    )
[109](https://docs.rs#109)}
[110](https://docs.rs#110)
[111](https://docs.rs#111)/// A module which is typically glob imported.

[115](https://docs.rs#115)/// ```

[122](https://docs.rs#122)    #[doc(hidden)]
[123](https://docs.rs#123)    pub use wasm_bindgen_macro::__wasm_bindgen_class_marker;
[124](https://docs.rs#124)    pub use wasm_bindgen_macro::wasm_bindgen;
[125](https://docs.rs#125)
[126](https://docs.rs#126)    pub use crate::JsError;
[127](https://docs.rs#127)}
[128](https://docs.rs#128)
[129](https://docs.rs#129)pub use wasm_bindgen_macro::link_to;
[130](https://docs.rs#130)
[131](https://docs.rs#131)pub mod closure;

[141](https://docs.rs#141)

[161](https://docs.rs#161)
[162](https://docs.rs#162)/// Representation of an object owned by JS.
[163](https://docs.rs#163)///
[164](https://docs.rs#164)/// A `JsValue` doesn't actually live in Rust right now but actually in a table
[165](https://docs.rs#165)/// owned by the `wasm-bindgen` generated JS glue code. Eventually the ownership
[166](https://docs.rs#166)/// will transfer into Wasm directly and this will likely become more efficient,
[167](https://docs.rs#167)/// but for now it may be slightly slow.
[168](https://docs.rs#168)pub struct JsValue {
[169](https://docs.rs#169)    idx: u32,
[170](https://docs.rs#170)    _marker: PhantomData<*mut u8>, // not at all threadsafe
[171](https://docs.rs#171)}
[172](https://docs.rs#172)
[173](https://docs.rs#173)#[cfg(not(target_feature = "atomics"))]
[174](https://docs.rs#174)unsafe impl Send for JsValue {}
[175](https://docs.rs#175)#[cfg(not(target_feature = "atomics"))]
[176](https://docs.rs#176)unsafe impl Sync for JsValue {}
[177](https://docs.rs#177)
[178](https://docs.rs#178)unsafe impl ErasableGeneric for JsValue {
[179](https://docs.rs#179)    type Repr = JsValue;
[180](https://docs.rs#180)}
[181](https://docs.rs#181)
[182](https://docs.rs#182)impl Promising for JsValue {
[183](https://docs.rs#183)    type Resolution = JsValue;
[184](https://docs.rs#184)}
[185](https://docs.rs#185)
[186](https://docs.rs#186)impl JsValue {
[187](https://docs.rs#187)    /// The `null` JS value constant.
[188](https://docs.rs#188)    pub const NULL: JsValue = JsValue::_new(__rt::JSIDX_NULL);
[189](https://docs.rs#189)
[190](https://docs.rs#190)    /// The `undefined` JS value constant.
[191](https://docs.rs#191)    pub const UNDEFINED: JsValue = JsValue::_new(__rt::JSIDX_UNDEFINED);
[192](https://docs.rs#192)
[193](https://docs.rs#193)    /// The `true` JS value constant.
[194](https://docs.rs#194)    pub const TRUE: JsValue = JsValue::_new(__rt::JSIDX_TRUE);
[195](https://docs.rs#195)
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    /// The `false` JS value constant.
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    pub const FALSE: JsValue = JsValue::_new(__rt::JSIDX_FALSE);
[198](https://docs.rs#198)
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    #[inline]
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    const fn _new(idx: u32) -> JsValue {
[201](https://docs.rs#201)        JsValue {
[202](https://docs.rs#202)            idx,
[203](https://docs.rs#203)            _marker: PhantomData,
[204](https://docs.rs#204)        }
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    }
[206](https://docs.rs#206)
[207](https://docs.rs#207)    /// Creates a new JS value which is a string.
[208](https://docs.rs#208)    ///
[209](https://docs.rs#209)    /// The utf-8 string provided is copied to the JS heap and the string will
[210](https://docs.rs#210)    /// be owned by the JS garbage collector.
[211](https://docs.rs#211)    #[allow(clippy::should_implement_trait)] // cannot fix without breaking change
[212](https://docs.rs#212)    #[inline]
[213](https://docs.rs#213)    pub fn from_str(s: &str) -> JsValue {
[214](https://docs.rs#214)        wbg_cast(s)
[215](https://docs.rs#215)    }
[216](https://docs.rs#216)
[217](https://docs.rs#217)    /// Creates a new JS value which is a number.
[218](https://docs.rs#218)    ///
[219](https://docs.rs#219)    /// This function creates a JS value representing a number (a heap
[220](https://docs.rs#220)    /// allocated number) and returns a handle to the JS version of it.
[221](https://docs.rs#221)    #[inline]
[222](https://docs.rs#222)    pub fn from_f64(n: f64) -> JsValue {
[223](https://docs.rs#223)        wbg_cast(n)
[224](https://docs.rs#224)    }
[225](https://docs.rs#225)
[226](https://docs.rs#226)    /// Creates a new JS value which is a bigint from a string representing a number.
[227](https://docs.rs#227)    ///
[228](https://docs.rs#228)    /// This function creates a JS value representing a bigint (a heap
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    /// allocated large integer) and returns a handle to the JS version of it.
[230](https://docs.rs#230)    #[inline]
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    pub fn bigint_from_str(s: &str) -> JsValue {
[232](https://docs.rs#232)        __wbindgen_bigint_from_str(s)
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    }
[234](https://docs.rs#234)
[235](https://docs.rs#235)    /// Creates a new JS value which is a boolean.
[236](https://docs.rs#236)    ///
[237](https://docs.rs#237)    /// This function creates a JS object representing a boolean (a heap
[238](https://docs.rs#238)    /// allocated boolean) and returns a handle to the JS version of it.
[239](https://docs.rs#239)    #[inline]
[240](https://docs.rs#240)    pub const fn from_bool(b: bool) -> JsValue {
[241](https://docs.rs#241)        if b {
[242](https://docs.rs#242)            JsValue::TRUE
[243](https://docs.rs#243)        } else {
[244](https://docs.rs#244)            JsValue::FALSE
[245](https://docs.rs#245)        }
[246](https://docs.rs#246)    }
[247](https://docs.rs#247)
[248](https://docs.rs#248)    /// Creates a new JS value representing `undefined`.
[249](https://docs.rs#249)    #[inline]
[250](https://docs.rs#250)    pub const fn undefined() -> JsValue {
[251](https://docs.rs#251)        JsValue::UNDEFINED
[252](https://docs.rs#252)    }
[253](https://docs.rs#253)
[254](https://docs.rs#254)    /// Creates a new JS value representing `null`.
[255](https://docs.rs#255)    #[inline]
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    pub const fn null() -> JsValue {
[257](https://docs.rs#257)        JsValue::NULL
[258](https://docs.rs#258)    }
[259](https://docs.rs#259)
[260](https://docs.rs#260)    /// Creates a new JS symbol with the optional description specified.
[261](https://docs.rs#261)    ///
[262](https://docs.rs#262)    /// This function will invoke the `Symbol` constructor in JS and return the
[263](https://docs.rs#263)    /// JS object corresponding to the symbol created.
[264](https://docs.rs#264)    pub fn symbol(description: Option<&str>) -> JsValue {
[265](https://docs.rs#265)        __wbindgen_symbol_new(description)
[266](https://docs.rs#266)    }
[267](https://docs.rs#267)
[268](https://docs.rs#268)    /// Creates a new `JsValue` from the JSON serialization of the object `t`
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    /// provided.
[270](https://docs.rs#270)    ///
[271](https://docs.rs#271)    /// **This function is deprecated**, due to [creating a dependency cycle in
[272](https://docs.rs#272)    /// some circumstances][dep-cycle-issue]. Use [`serde-wasm-bindgen`] or
[273](https://docs.rs#273)    /// [`gloo_utils::format::JsValueSerdeExt`] instead.
[274](https://docs.rs#274)    ///
[275](https://docs.rs#275)    /// [dep-cycle-issue]: https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen/issues/2770
[276](https://docs.rs#276)    /// [`serde-wasm-bindgen`]: https://docs.rs/serde-wasm-bindgen
[277](https://docs.rs#277)    /// [`gloo_utils::format::JsValueSerdeExt`]: https://docs.rs/gloo-utils/latest/gloo_utils/format/trait.JsValueSerdeExt.html
[278](https://docs.rs#278)    ///
[279](https://docs.rs#279)    /// This function will serialize the provided value `t` to a JSON string,
[280](https://docs.rs#280)    /// send the JSON string to JS, parse it into a JS object, and then return
[281](https://docs.rs#281)    /// a handle to the JS object. This is unlikely to be super speedy so it's
[282](https://docs.rs#282)    /// not recommended for large payloads, but it's a nice to have in some
[283](https://docs.rs#283)    /// situations!
[284](https://docs.rs#284)    ///
[285](https://docs.rs#285)    /// Usage of this API requires activating the `serde-serialize` feature of
[286](https://docs.rs#286)    /// the `wasm-bindgen` crate.
[287](https://docs.rs#287)    ///
[288](https://docs.rs#288)    /// # Errors
[289](https://docs.rs#289)    ///
[290](https://docs.rs#290)    /// Returns any error encountered when serializing `T` into JSON.
[291](https://docs.rs#291)    #[cfg(feature = "serde-serialize")]
[292](https://docs.rs#292)    #[deprecated = "causes dependency cycles, use `serde-wasm-bindgen` or `gloo_utils::format::JsValueSerdeExt` instead"]
[293](https://docs.rs#293)    pub fn from_serde<T>(t: &T) -> serde_json::Result<JsValue>
[294](https://docs.rs#294)    where
[295](https://docs.rs#295)        T: serde::ser::Serialize + ?Sized,
[296](https://docs.rs#296)    {
[297](https://docs.rs#297)        let s = serde_json::to_string(t)?;
[298](https://docs.rs#298)        Ok(__wbindgen_json_parse(s))
[299](https://docs.rs#299)    }
[300](https://docs.rs#300)
[301](https://docs.rs#301)    /// Invokes `JSON.stringify` on this value and then parses the resulting
[302](https://docs.rs#302)    /// JSON into an arbitrary Rust value.
[303](https://docs.rs#303)    ///
[304](https://docs.rs#304)    /// **This function is deprecated**, due to [creating a dependency cycle in
[305](https://docs.rs#305)    /// some circumstances][dep-cycle-issue]. Use [`serde-wasm-bindgen`] or
[306](https://docs.rs#306)    /// [`gloo_utils::format::JsValueSerdeExt`] instead.
[307](https://docs.rs#307)    ///
[308](https://docs.rs#308)    /// [dep-cycle-issue]: https://github.com/wasm-bindgen/wasm-bindgen/issues/2770
[309](https://docs.rs#309)    /// [`serde-wasm-bindgen`]: https://docs.rs/serde-wasm-bindgen
[310](https://docs.rs#310)    /// [`gloo_utils::format::JsValueSerdeExt`]: https://docs.rs/gloo-utils/latest/gloo_utils/format/trait.JsValueSerdeExt.html
[311](https://docs.rs#311)    ///
[312](https://docs.rs#312)    /// This function will first call `JSON.stringify` on the `JsValue` itself.
[313](https://docs.rs#313)    /// The resulting string is then passed into Rust which then parses it as
[314](https://docs.rs#314)    /// JSON into the resulting value.
[315](https://docs.rs#315)    ///
[316](https://docs.rs#316)    /// Usage of this API requires activating the `serde-serialize` feature of
[317](https://docs.rs#317)    /// the `wasm-bindgen` crate.
[318](https://docs.rs#318)    ///
[319](https://docs.rs#319)    /// # Errors
[320](https://docs.rs#320)    ///
[321](https://docs.rs#321)    /// Returns any error encountered when parsing the JSON into a `T`.
[322](https://docs.rs#322)    #[cfg(feature = "serde-serialize")]
[323](https://docs.rs#323)    #[deprecated = "causes dependency cycles, use `serde-wasm-bindgen` or `gloo_utils::format::JsValueSerdeExt` instead"]
[324](https://docs.rs#324)    pub fn into_serde<T>(&self) -> serde_json::Result<T>
[325](https://docs.rs#325)    where
[326](https://docs.rs#326)        T: for<'a> serde::de::Deserialize<'a>,
[327](https://docs.rs#327)    {
[328](https://docs.rs#328)        let s = __wbindgen_json_serialize(self);
[329](https://docs.rs#329)        // Turns out `JSON.stringify(undefined) === undefined`, so if
[330](https://docs.rs#330)        // we're passed `undefined` reinterpret it as `null` for JSON
[331](https://docs.rs#331)        // purposes.
[332](https://docs.rs#332)        serde_json::from_str(s.as_deref().unwrap_or("null"))
[333](https://docs.rs#333)    }
[334](https://docs.rs#334)
[335](https://docs.rs#335)    /// Returns the `f64` value of this JS value if it's an instance of a
[336](https://docs.rs#336)    /// number.
[337](https://docs.rs#337)    ///
[338](https://docs.rs#338)    /// If this JS value is not an instance of a number then this returns
[339](https://docs.rs#339)    /// `None`.
[340](https://docs.rs#340)    #[inline]
[341](https://docs.rs#341)    pub fn as_f64(&self) -> Option<f64> {
[342](https://docs.rs#342)        __wbindgen_number_get(self)
[343](https://docs.rs#343)    }
[344](https://docs.rs#344)
[345](https://docs.rs#345)    /// Tests whether this JS value is a JS string.
[346](https://docs.rs#346)    #[inline]
[347](https://docs.rs#347)    pub fn is_string(&self) -> bool {
[348](https://docs.rs#348)        __wbindgen_is_string(self)
[349](https://docs.rs#349)    }
[350](https://docs.rs#350)
[351](https://docs.rs#351)    /// If this JS value is a string value, this function copies the JS string
[352](https://docs.rs#352)    /// value into Wasm linear memory, encoded as UTF-8, and returns it as a
[353](https://docs.rs#353)    /// Rust `String`.
[354](https://docs.rs#354)    ///
[355](https://docs.rs#355)    /// To avoid the copying and re-encoding, consider the
[356](https://docs.rs#356)    /// `JsString::try_from()` function from [js-sys](https://docs.rs/js-sys)
[357](https://docs.rs#357)    /// instead.
[358](https://docs.rs#358)    ///
[359](https://docs.rs#359)    /// If this JS value is not an instance of a string or if it's not valid
[360](https://docs.rs#360)    /// utf-8 then this returns `None`.
[361](https://docs.rs#361)    ///
[362](https://docs.rs#362)    /// # UTF-16 vs UTF-8
[363](https://docs.rs#363)    ///
[364](https://docs.rs#364)    /// JavaScript strings in general are encoded as UTF-16, but Rust strings
[365](https://docs.rs#365)    /// are encoded as UTF-8. This can cause the Rust string to look a bit
[366](https://docs.rs#366)    /// different than the JS string sometimes. For more details see the
[367](https://docs.rs#367)    /// [documentation about the `str` type][caveats] which contains a few
[368](https://docs.rs#368)    /// caveats about the encodings.
[369](https://docs.rs#369)    ///
[370](https://docs.rs#370)    /// [caveats]: https://wasm-bindgen.github.io/wasm-bindgen/reference/types/str.html
[371](https://docs.rs#371)    #[inline]
[372](https://docs.rs#372)    pub fn as_string(&self) -> Option<String> {
[373](https://docs.rs#373)        __wbindgen_string_get(self)
[374](https://docs.rs#374)    }
[375](https://docs.rs#375)
[376](https://docs.rs#376)    /// Returns the `bool` value of this JS value if it's an instance of a
[377](https://docs.rs#377)    /// boolean.
[378](https://docs.rs#378)    ///
[379](https://docs.rs#379)    /// If this JS value is not an instance of a boolean then this returns
[380](https://docs.rs#380)    /// `None`.
[381](https://docs.rs#381)    #[inline]
[382](https://docs.rs#382)    pub fn as_bool(&self) -> Option<bool> {
[383](https://docs.rs#383)        __wbindgen_boolean_get(self)
[384](https://docs.rs#384)    }

[434](https://docs.rs#434)    /// Applies the unary `typeof` JS operator on a `JsValue`.

[441](https://docs.rs#441)

[597](https://docs.rs#597)
[598](https://docs.rs#598)macro_rules! forward_deref_unop {
[599](https://docs.rs#599)    (impl $imp:ident, $method:ident for $t:ty) => {
[600](https://docs.rs#600)        impl $imp for $t {
[601](https://docs.rs#601)            type Output = <&'static $t as $imp>::Output;
[602](https://docs.rs#602)
[603](https://docs.rs#603)            #[inline]
[604](https://docs.rs#604)            fn $method(self) -> <&'static $t as $imp>::Output {
[605](https://docs.rs#605)                $imp::$method(&self)
[606](https://docs.rs#606)            }
[607](https://docs.rs#607)        }
[608](https://docs.rs#608)    };
[609](https://docs.rs#609)}
[610](https://docs.rs#610)
[611](https://docs.rs#611)macro_rules! forward_deref_binop {
[612](https://docs.rs#612)    (impl $imp:ident, $method:ident for $t:ty) => {
[613](https://docs.rs#613)        impl<'a> $imp<$t> for &'a $t {
[614](https://docs.rs#614)            type Output = <&'static $t as $imp<&'static $t>>::Output;
[615](https://docs.rs#615)
[616](https://docs.rs#616)            #[inline]
[617](https://docs.rs#617)            fn $method(self, other: $t) -> <&'static $t as $imp<&'static $t>>::Output {
[618](https://docs.rs#618)                $imp::$method(self, &other)
[619](https://docs.rs#619)            }
[620](https://docs.rs#620)        }
[621](https://docs.rs#621)
[622](https://docs.rs#622)        impl $imp<&$t> for $t {
[623](https://docs.rs#623)            type Output = <&'static $t as $imp<&'static $t>>::Output;
[624](https://docs.rs#624)
[625](https://docs.rs#625)            #[inline]
[626](https://docs.rs#626)            fn $method(self, other: &$t) -> <&'static $t as $imp<&'static $t>>::Output {
[627](https://docs.rs#627)                $imp::$method(&self, other)
[628](https://docs.rs#628)            }
[629](https://docs.rs#629)        }
[630](https://docs.rs#630)
[631](https://docs.rs#631)        impl $imp<$t> for $t {
[632](https://docs.rs#632)            type Output = <&'static $t as $imp<&'static $t>>::Output;
[633](https://docs.rs#633)
[634](https://docs.rs#634)            #[inline]
[635](https://docs.rs#635)            fn $method(self, other: $t) -> <&'static $t as $imp<&'static $t>>::Output {
[636](https://docs.rs#636)                $imp::$method(&self, &other)
[637](https://docs.rs#637)            }
[638](https://docs.rs#638)        }
[639](https://docs.rs#639)    };
[640](https://docs.rs#640)}

[656](https://docs.rs#656)impl TryFrom<JsValue> for f64 {
[657](https://docs.rs#657)    type Error = JsValue;
[658](https://docs.rs#658)
[659](https://docs.rs#659)    /// Applies the unary `+` JS operator on a `JsValue`.
[660](https://docs.rs#660)    /// Returns the numeric result on success, or the JS error value on error.
[661](https://docs.rs#661)    ///
[662](https://docs.rs#662)    /// [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/Unary_plus)
[663](https://docs.rs#663)    #[inline]
[664](https://docs.rs#664)    fn try_from(val: JsValue) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
[665](https://docs.rs#665)        f64::try_from(&val)
[666](https://docs.rs#666)    }
[667](https://docs.rs#667)}
[668](https://docs.rs#668)
[669](https://docs.rs#669)impl TryFrom<&JsValue> for f64 {
[670](https://docs.rs#670)    type Error = JsValue;
[671](https://docs.rs#671)
[672](https://docs.rs#672)    /// Applies the unary `+` JS operator on a `JsValue`.
[673](https://docs.rs#673)    /// Returns the numeric result on success, or the JS error value on error.
[674](https://docs.rs#674)    ///
[675](https://docs.rs#675)    /// [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Operators/Unary_plus)
[676](https://docs.rs#676)    #[inline]
[677](https://docs.rs#677)    fn try_from(val: &JsValue) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
[678](https://docs.rs#678)        let jsval = __wbindgen_try_into_number(val);
[679](https://docs.rs#679)        match jsval.as_f64() {
[680](https://docs.rs#680)            Some(num) => Ok(num),
[681](https://docs.rs#681)            None => Err(jsval),
[682](https://docs.rs#682)        }
[683](https://docs.rs#683)    }
[684](https://docs.rs#684)}

[1054](https://docs.rs#1054)        impl TryFrom<JsValue> for $n {
[1055](https://docs.rs#1055)            type Error = JsValue;
[1056](https://docs.rs#1056)
[1057](https://docs.rs#1057)            #[inline]
[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)            fn try_from(v: JsValue) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)                Self::try_from_js_value(v)
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)            }
[1061](https://docs.rs#1061)        }
[1062](https://docs.rs#1062)
[1063](https://docs.rs#1063)        impl TryFromJsValue for $n {
[1064](https://docs.rs#1064)            #[inline]
[1065](https://docs.rs#1065)            fn try_from_js_value_ref(val: &JsValue) -> Option<$n> {
[1066](https://docs.rs#1066)                let as_i64 = __wbindgen_bigint_get_as_i64(&val)?;
[1067](https://docs.rs#1067)                // Reinterpret bits; ABI-wise this is safe to do and allows us to avoid
[1068](https://docs.rs#1068)                // having separate intrinsics per signed/unsigned types.
[1069](https://docs.rs#1069)                let as_self = as_i64 as $n;
[1070](https://docs.rs#1070)                // Double-check that we didn't truncate the bigint to 64 bits.
[1071](https://docs.rs#1071)                if val == &as_self {
[1072](https://docs.rs#1072)                    Some(as_self)
[1073](https://docs.rs#1073)                } else {
[1074](https://docs.rs#1074)                    None
[1075](https://docs.rs#1075)                }
[1076](https://docs.rs#1076)            }
[1077](https://docs.rs#1077)        }
[1078](https://docs.rs#1078)    )*)

[1083](https://docs.rs#1083)macro_rules! num128 {
[1084](https://docs.rs#1084)    ($ty:ty, $hi_ty:ty) => {
[1085](https://docs.rs#1085)        impl PartialEq<$ty> for JsValue {
[1086](https://docs.rs#1086)            #[inline]
[1087](https://docs.rs#1087)            fn eq(&self, other: &$ty) -> bool {
[1088](https://docs.rs#1088)                self == &JsValue::from(*other)
[1089](https://docs.rs#1089)            }
[1090](https://docs.rs#1090)        }
[1091](https://docs.rs#1091)
[1092](https://docs.rs#1092)        impl From<$ty> for JsValue {
[1093](https://docs.rs#1093)            #[inline]
[1094](https://docs.rs#1094)            fn from(arg: $ty) -> JsValue {
[1095](https://docs.rs#1095)                wbg_cast(arg)
[1096](https://docs.rs#1096)            }
[1097](https://docs.rs#1097)        }
[1098](https://docs.rs#1098)
[1099](https://docs.rs#1099)        impl TryFrom<JsValue> for $ty {
[1100](https://docs.rs#1100)            type Error = JsValue;
[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)
[1102](https://docs.rs#1102)            #[inline]
[1103](https://docs.rs#1103)            fn try_from(v: JsValue) -> Result<Self, JsValue> {
[1104](https://docs.rs#1104)                Self::try_from_js_value(v)
[1105](https://docs.rs#1105)            }
[1106](https://docs.rs#1106)        }
[1107](https://docs.rs#1107)
[1108](https://docs.rs#1108)        impl TryFromJsValue for $ty {
[1109](https://docs.rs#1109)            // This is a non-standard Wasm bindgen conversion, supported equally
[1110](https://docs.rs#1110)            fn try_from_js_value_ref(v: &JsValue) -> Option<$ty> {
[1111](https://docs.rs#1111)                // Truncate the bigint to 64 bits, this will give us the lower part.
[1112](https://docs.rs#1112)                // The lower part must be interpreted as unsigned in both i128 and u128.
[1113](https://docs.rs#1113)                let lo = __wbindgen_bigint_get_as_i64(&v)? as u64;
[1114](https://docs.rs#1114)                // Now we know it's a bigint, so we can safely use `>> 64n` without
[1115](https://docs.rs#1115)                // worrying about a JS exception on type mismatch.
[1116](https://docs.rs#1116)                let hi = v >> JsValue::from(64_u64);
[1117](https://docs.rs#1117)                // The high part is the one we want checked against a 64-bit range.
[1118](https://docs.rs#1118)                // If it fits, then our original number is in the 128-bit range.
[1119](https://docs.rs#1119)                <$hi_ty>::try_from_js_value_ref(&hi).map(|hi| Self::from(hi) << 64 | Self::from(lo))
[1120](https://docs.rs#1120)            }
[1121](https://docs.rs#1121)        }
[1122](https://docs.rs#1122)    };
[1123](https://docs.rs#1123)}

[1139](https://docs.rs#1139)impl<T: TryFromJsValue> TryFromJsValue for Option<T> {
[1140](https://docs.rs#1140)    fn try_from_js_value_ref(value: &JsValue) -> Option<Self> {
[1141](https://docs.rs#1141)        if value.is_undefined() {
[1142](https://docs.rs#1142)            Some(None)
[1143](https://docs.rs#1143)        } else {
[1144](https://docs.rs#1144)            T::try_from_js_value_ref(value).map(Some)
[1145](https://docs.rs#1145)        }
[1146](https://docs.rs#1146)    }
[1147](https://docs.rs#1147)}
[1148](https://docs.rs#1148)
[1149](https://docs.rs#1149)// Converts a JS `Array` whose elements all convert via `T::try_from_js_value`.
[1150](https://docs.rs#1150)// Rejects non-array values and arrays containing any element that fails to
[1151](https://docs.rs#1151)// convert. Mirrors the `Array`-shaped representation used by the static ABI
[1152](https://docs.rs#1152)// path in `js_value_vector_from_abi`.
[1153](https://docs.rs#1153)impl<T: TryFromJsValue> TryFromJsValue for Vec<T> {
[1154](https://docs.rs#1154)    fn try_from_js_value_ref(value: &JsValue) -> Option<Self> {
[1155](https://docs.rs#1155)        if !__wbindgen_is_array(value) {
[1156](https://docs.rs#1156)            return None;
[1157](https://docs.rs#1157)        }
[1158](https://docs.rs#1158)        let len = __wbindgen_reflect_get(value, &JsValue::from_str("length")).as_f64()? as u32;
[1159](https://docs.rs#1159)        let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(len as usize);
[1160](https://docs.rs#1160)        for i in 0..len {
[1161](https://docs.rs#1161)            let elem = __wbindgen_reflect_get(value, &JsValue::from_f64(i as f64));
[1162](https://docs.rs#1162)            out.push(T::try_from_js_value(elem).ok()?);
[1163](https://docs.rs#1163)        }
[1164](https://docs.rs#1164)        Some(out)
[1165](https://docs.rs#1165)    }
[1166](https://docs.rs#1166)}
[1167](https://docs.rs#1167)
[1168](https://docs.rs#1168)// `usize` and `isize` use the public pointer-sized JS number ABI, which is

[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)    }

[1324](https://docs.rs#1324)    fn clone(&self) -> JsValue {
[1325](https://docs.rs#1325)        JsValue::_new(unsafe { __wbindgen_object_clone_ref(self.idx) })
[1326](https://docs.rs#1326)    }

[1332](https://docs.rs#1332)    }

[1334](https://docs.rs#1334)
[1335](https://docs.rs#1335)impl Drop for JsValue {
[1336](https://docs.rs#1336)    #[inline]
[1337](https://docs.rs#1337)    fn drop(&mut self) {
[1338](https://docs.rs#1338)        unsafe {
[1339](https://docs.rs#1339)            // We definitely should never drop anything in the stack area
[1340](https://docs.rs#1340)            debug_assert!(
[1341](https://docs.rs#1341)                self.idx >= __rt::JSIDX_OFFSET,
[1342](https://docs.rs#1342)                "free of stack slot {}",
[1343](https://docs.rs#1343)                self.idx
[1344](https://docs.rs#1344)            );
[1345](https://docs.rs#1345)
[1346](https://docs.rs#1346)            // Otherwise if we're not dropping one of our reserved values,
[1347](https://docs.rs#1347)            // actually call the intrinsic. See #1054 for eventually removing
[1348](https://docs.rs#1348)            // this branch.
[1349](https://docs.rs#1349)            if self.idx >= __rt::JSIDX_RESERVED {
[1350](https://docs.rs#1350)                __wbindgen_object_drop_ref(self.idx);
[1351](https://docs.rs#1351)            }
[1352](https://docs.rs#1352)        }
[1353](https://docs.rs#1353)    }
[1354](https://docs.rs#1354)}
[1355](https://docs.rs#1355)

[1357](https://docs.rs#1357)    fn default() -> Self {
[1358](https://docs.rs#1358)        Self::UNDEFINED
[1359](https://docs.rs#1359)    }

[1361](https://docs.rs#1361)
[1362](https://docs.rs#1362)/// Wrapper type for imported statics.
[1363](https://docs.rs#1363)///
[1364](https://docs.rs#1364)/// This type is used whenever a `static` is imported from a JS module, for
[1365](https://docs.rs#1365)/// example this import:
[1366](https://docs.rs#1366)///
[1367](https://docs.rs#1367)/// ```ignore
[1368](https://docs.rs#1368)/// #[wasm_bindgen]
[1369](https://docs.rs#1369)/// extern "C" {
[1370](https://docs.rs#1370)///     static console: JsValue;
[1371](https://docs.rs#1371)/// }
[1372](https://docs.rs#1372)/// ```
[1373](https://docs.rs#1373)///
[1374](https://docs.rs#1374)/// will generate in Rust a value that looks like:
[1375](https://docs.rs#1375)///
[1376](https://docs.rs#1376)/// ```ignore
[1377](https://docs.rs#1377)/// static console: JsStatic<JsValue> = ...;
[1378](https://docs.rs#1378)/// ```
[1379](https://docs.rs#1379)///
[1380](https://docs.rs#1380)/// This type implements `Deref` to the inner type so it's typically used as if
[1381](https://docs.rs#1381)/// it were `&T`.
[1382](https://docs.rs#1382)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[1383](https://docs.rs#1383)#[deprecated = "use with `#[wasm_bindgen(thread_local_v2)]` instead"]
[1384](https://docs.rs#1384)pub struct JsStatic<T: 'static> {
[1385](https://docs.rs#1385)    #[doc(hidden)]
[1386](https://docs.rs#1386)    pub __inner: &'static std::thread::LocalKey<T>,
[1387](https://docs.rs#1387)}
[1388](https://docs.rs#1388)
[1389](https://docs.rs#1389)#[cfg(feature = "std")]
[1390](https://docs.rs#1390)#[allow(deprecated)]
[1391](https://docs.rs#1391)#[cfg(not(target_feature = "atomics"))]
[1392](https://docs.rs#1392)impl<T: crate::convert::FromWasmAbi + 'static> Deref for JsStatic<T> {
[1393](https://docs.rs#1393)    type Target = T;
[1394](https://docs.rs#1394)    fn deref(&self) -> &T {
[1395](https://docs.rs#1395)        unsafe { self.__inner.with(|ptr| &*(ptr as *const T)) }
[1396](https://docs.rs#1396)    }
[1397](https://docs.rs#1397)}
[1398](https://docs.rs#1398)
[1399](https://docs.rs#1399)/// Wrapper type for imported statics.
[1400](https://docs.rs#1400)///
[1401](https://docs.rs#1401)/// This type is used whenever a `static` is imported from a JS module, for
[1402](https://docs.rs#1402)/// example this import:
[1403](https://docs.rs#1403)///
[1404](https://docs.rs#1404)/// ```ignore
[1405](https://docs.rs#1405)/// #[wasm_bindgen]
[1406](https://docs.rs#1406)/// extern "C" {
[1407](https://docs.rs#1407)///     #[wasm_bindgen(thread_local_v2)]
[1408](https://docs.rs#1408)///     static console: JsValue;
[1409](https://docs.rs#1409)/// }
[1410](https://docs.rs#1410)/// ```
[1411](https://docs.rs#1411)///
[1412](https://docs.rs#1412)/// will generate in Rust a value that looks like:
[1413](https://docs.rs#1413)///
[1414](https://docs.rs#1414)/// ```ignore
[1415](https://docs.rs#1415)/// static console: JsThreadLocal<JsValue> = ...;
[1416](https://docs.rs#1416)/// ```
[1417](https://docs.rs#1417)pub struct JsThreadLocal<T: 'static> {
[1418](https://docs.rs#1418)    #[doc(hidden)]
[1419](https://docs.rs#1419)    #[cfg(not(target_feature = "atomics"))]
[1420](https://docs.rs#1420)    pub __inner: &'static __rt::LazyCell<T>,
[1421](https://docs.rs#1421)    #[doc(hidden)]
[1422](https://docs.rs#1422)    #[cfg(target_feature = "atomics")]
[1423](https://docs.rs#1423)    pub __inner: fn() -> *const T,
[1424](https://docs.rs#1424)}
[1425](https://docs.rs#1425)
[1426](https://docs.rs#1426)impl<T> JsThreadLocal<T> {
[1427](https://docs.rs#1427)    pub fn with<F, R>(&'static self, f: F) -> R
[1428](https://docs.rs#1428)    where
[1429](https://docs.rs#1429)        F: FnOnce(&T) -> R,
[1430](https://docs.rs#1430)    {
[1431](https://docs.rs#1431)        #[cfg(not(target_feature = "atomics"))]
[1432](https://docs.rs#1432)        return f(self.__inner);
[1433](https://docs.rs#1433)        #[cfg(target_feature = "atomics")]
[1434](https://docs.rs#1434)        f(unsafe { &*(self.__inner)() })
[1435](https://docs.rs#1435)    }
[1436](https://docs.rs#1436)}
[1437](https://docs.rs#1437)
[1438](https://docs.rs#1438)#[cold]
[1439](https://docs.rs#1439)#[inline(never)]
[1440](https://docs.rs#1440)#[deprecated(note = "renamed to `throw_str`")]
[1441](https://docs.rs#1441)#[doc(hidden)]
[1442](https://docs.rs#1442)pub fn throw(s: &str) -> ! {
[1443](https://docs.rs#1443)    throw_str(s)
[1444](https://docs.rs#1444)}
[1445](https://docs.rs#1445)
[1446](https://docs.rs#1446)/// Throws a JS exception.
[1447](https://docs.rs#1447)///
[1448](https://docs.rs#1448)/// This function will throw a JS exception with the message provided. The
[1449](https://docs.rs#1449)/// function will not return as the Wasm stack will be popped when the exception
[1450](https://docs.rs#1450)/// is thrown.
[1451](https://docs.rs#1451)///
[1452](https://docs.rs#1452)/// Note that it is very easy to leak memory with this function because this
[1453](https://docs.rs#1453)/// function, unlike `panic!` on other platforms, **will not run destructors**.
[1454](https://docs.rs#1454)/// It's recommended to return a `Result` where possible to avoid the worry of
[1455](https://docs.rs#1455)/// leaks.
[1456](https://docs.rs#1456)///
[1457](https://docs.rs#1457)/// If you need destructors to run, consider using `panic!` when building with
[1458](https://docs.rs#1458)/// `-Cpanic=unwind`. If the `std` feature is used panics will be caught at the
[1459](https://docs.rs#1459)/// JavaScript boundary and converted to JavaScript exceptions.
[1460](https://docs.rs#1460)#[cold]
[1461](https://docs.rs#1461)#[inline(never)]
[1462](https://docs.rs#1462)pub fn throw_str(s: &str) -> ! {
[1463](https://docs.rs#1463)    __wbindgen_throw(s);
[1464](https://docs.rs#1464)    unsafe { core::hint::unreachable_unchecked() }
[1465](https://docs.rs#1465)}
[1466](https://docs.rs#1466)
[1467](https://docs.rs#1467)/// Rethrow a JS exception
[1468](https://docs.rs#1468)///
[1469](https://docs.rs#1469)/// This function will throw a JS exception with the JS value provided. This
[1470](https://docs.rs#1470)/// function will not return and the Wasm stack will be popped until the point
[1471](https://docs.rs#1471)/// of entry of Wasm itself.
[1472](https://docs.rs#1472)///
[1473](https://docs.rs#1473)/// Note that it is very easy to leak memory with this function because this
[1474](https://docs.rs#1474)/// function, unlike `panic!` on other platforms, **will not run destructors**.
[1475](https://docs.rs#1475)/// It's recommended to return a `Result` where possible to avoid the worry of
[1476](https://docs.rs#1476)/// leaks.
[1477](https://docs.rs#1477)///
[1478](https://docs.rs#1478)/// If you need destructors to run, consider using `panic!` when building with
[1479](https://docs.rs#1479)/// `-Cpanic=unwind`. If the `std` feature is used panics will be caught at the
[1480](https://docs.rs#1480)/// JavaScript boundary and converted to JavaScript exceptions.
[1481](https://docs.rs#1481)#[cold]
[1482](https://docs.rs#1482)#[inline(never)]
[1483](https://docs.rs#1483)pub fn throw_val(s: JsValue) -> ! {
[1484](https://docs.rs#1484)    __wbindgen_rethrow(s);
[1485](https://docs.rs#1485)    unsafe { core::hint::unreachable_unchecked() }
[1486](https://docs.rs#1486)}
[1487](https://docs.rs#1487)
[1488](https://docs.rs#1488)/// Get the count of live `externref`s / `JsValue`s in `wasm-bindgen`'s heap.
[1489](https://docs.rs#1489)///
[1490](https://docs.rs#1490)/// ## Usage
[1491](https://docs.rs#1491)///
[1492](https://docs.rs#1492)/// This is intended for debugging and writing tests.
[1493](https://docs.rs#1493)///
[1494](https://docs.rs#1494)/// To write a test that asserts against unnecessarily keeping `anref`s /
[1495](https://docs.rs#1495)/// `JsValue`s alive:
[1496](https://docs.rs#1496)///
[1497](https://docs.rs#1497)/// * get an initial live count,
[1498](https://docs.rs#1498)///
[1499](https://docs.rs#1499)/// * perform some series of operations or function calls that should clean up
[1500](https://docs.rs#1500)///   after themselves, and should not keep holding onto `externref`s / `JsValue`s
[1501](https://docs.rs#1501)///   after completion,
[1502](https://docs.rs#1502)///
[1503](https://docs.rs#1503)/// * get the final live count,
[1504](https://docs.rs#1504)///
[1505](https://docs.rs#1505)/// * and assert that the initial and final counts are the same.
[1506](https://docs.rs#1506)///
[1507](https://docs.rs#1507)/// ## What is Counted
[1508](https://docs.rs#1508)///
[1509](https://docs.rs#1509)/// Note that this only counts the *owned* `externref`s / `JsValue`s that end up in
[1510](https://docs.rs#1510)/// `wasm-bindgen`'s heap. It does not count borrowed `externref`s / `JsValue`s
[1511](https://docs.rs#1511)/// that are on its stack.
[1512](https://docs.rs#1512)///
[1513](https://docs.rs#1513)/// For example, these `JsValue`s are accounted for:
[1514](https://docs.rs#1514)///
[1515](https://docs.rs#1515)/// ```ignore
[1516](https://docs.rs#1516)/// #[wasm_bindgen]
[1517](https://docs.rs#1517)/// pub fn my_function(this_is_counted: JsValue) {
[1518](https://docs.rs#1518)///     let also_counted = JsValue::from_str("hi");
[1519](https://docs.rs#1519)///     assert!(wasm_bindgen::externref_heap_live_count() >= 2);
[1520](https://docs.rs#1520)/// }
[1521](https://docs.rs#1521)/// ```
[1522](https://docs.rs#1522)///
[1523](https://docs.rs#1523)/// While this borrowed `JsValue` ends up on the stack, not the heap, and
[1524](https://docs.rs#1524)/// therefore is not accounted for:
[1525](https://docs.rs#1525)///
[1526](https://docs.rs#1526)/// ```ignore
[1527](https://docs.rs#1527)/// #[wasm_bindgen]
[1528](https://docs.rs#1528)/// pub fn my_other_function(this_is_not_counted: &JsValue) {
[1529](https://docs.rs#1529)///     // ...
[1530](https://docs.rs#1530)/// }
[1531](https://docs.rs#1531)/// ```
[1532](https://docs.rs#1532)pub fn externref_heap_live_count() -> u32 {
[1533](https://docs.rs#1533)    __wbindgen_externref_heap_live_count()
[1534](https://docs.rs#1534)}
[1535](https://docs.rs#1535)
[1536](https://docs.rs#1536)#[doc(hidden)]
[1537](https://docs.rs#1537)pub fn anyref_heap_live_count() -> u32 {
[1538](https://docs.rs#1538)    externref_heap_live_count()
[1539](https://docs.rs#1539)}
[1540](https://docs.rs#1540)
[1541](https://docs.rs#1541)/// An extension trait for `Option<T>` and `Result<T, E>` for unwrapping the `T`
[1542](https://docs.rs#1542)/// value, or throwing a JS error if it is not available.
[1543](https://docs.rs#1543)///
[1544](https://docs.rs#1544)/// These methods should have a smaller code size footprint than the normal
[1545](https://docs.rs#1545)/// `Option::unwrap` and `Option::expect` methods, but they are specific to
[1546](https://docs.rs#1546)/// working with Wasm and JS.
[1547](https://docs.rs#1547)///
[1548](https://docs.rs#1548)/// On non-wasm32 targets, defaults to the normal unwrap/expect calls.
[1549](https://docs.rs#1549)///
[1550](https://docs.rs#1550)/// # Example
[1551](https://docs.rs#1551)///
[1552](https://docs.rs#1552)/// ```
[1553](https://docs.rs#1553)/// use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
[1554](https://docs.rs#1554)///
[1555](https://docs.rs#1555)/// // If the value is `Option::Some` or `Result::Ok`, then we just get the
[1556](https://docs.rs#1556)/// // contained `T` value.
[1557](https://docs.rs#1557)/// let x = Some(42);
[1558](https://docs.rs#1558)/// assert_eq!(x.unwrap_throw(), 42);
[1559](https://docs.rs#1559)///
[1560](https://docs.rs#1560)/// let y: Option<i32> = None;
[1561](https://docs.rs#1561)///
[1562](https://docs.rs#1562)/// // This call would throw an error to JS!
[1563](https://docs.rs#1563)/// //
[1564](https://docs.rs#1564)/// //     y.unwrap_throw()
[1565](https://docs.rs#1565)/// //
[1566](https://docs.rs#1566)/// // And this call would throw an error to JS with a custom error message!
[1567](https://docs.rs#1567)/// //
[1568](https://docs.rs#1568)/// //     y.expect_throw("woopsie daisy!")
[1569](https://docs.rs#1569)/// ```
[1570](https://docs.rs#1570)pub trait UnwrapThrowExt<T>: Sized {
[1571](https://docs.rs#1571)    /// Unwrap this `Option` or `Result`, but instead of panicking on failure,
[1572](https://docs.rs#1572)    /// throw an exception to JavaScript.
[1573](https://docs.rs#1573)    #[cfg_attr(
[1574](https://docs.rs#1574)        any(
[1575](https://docs.rs#1575)            debug_assertions,
[1576](https://docs.rs#1576)            not(all(target_family = "wasm", not(target_os = "wasi")))
[1577](https://docs.rs#1577)        ),
[1578](https://docs.rs#1578)        track_caller
[1579](https://docs.rs#1579)    )]
[1580](https://docs.rs#1580)    fn unwrap_throw(self) -> T {
[1581](https://docs.rs#1581)        if cfg!(all(
[1582](https://docs.rs#1582)            debug_assertions,
[1583](https://docs.rs#1583)            all(target_family = "wasm", not(target_os = "wasi"))
[1584](https://docs.rs#1584)        )) {
[1585](https://docs.rs#1585)            let loc = core::panic::Location::caller();
[1586](https://docs.rs#1586)            let msg = alloc::format!(
[1587](https://docs.rs#1587)                "called `{}::unwrap_throw()` ({}:{}:{})",
[1588](https://docs.rs#1588)                core::any::type_name::<Self>(),
[1589](https://docs.rs#1589)                loc.file(),
[1590](https://docs.rs#1590)                loc.line(),
[1591](https://docs.rs#1591)                loc.column()
[1592](https://docs.rs#1592)            );
[1593](https://docs.rs#1593)            self.expect_throw(&msg)
[1594](https://docs.rs#1594)        } else {
[1595](https://docs.rs#1595)            self.expect_throw("called `unwrap_throw()`")
[1596](https://docs.rs#1596)        }
[1597](https://docs.rs#1597)    }
[1598](https://docs.rs#1598)
[1599](https://docs.rs#1599)    /// Unwrap this container's `T` value, or throw an error to JS with the
[1600](https://docs.rs#1600)    /// given message if the `T` value is unavailable (e.g. an `Option<T>` is
[1601](https://docs.rs#1601)    /// `None`).
[1602](https://docs.rs#1602)    #[cfg_attr(
[1603](https://docs.rs#1603)        any(
[1604](https://docs.rs#1604)            debug_assertions,
[1605](https://docs.rs#1605)            not(all(target_family = "wasm", not(target_os = "wasi")))
[1606](https://docs.rs#1606)        ),
[1607](https://docs.rs#1607)        track_caller
[1608](https://docs.rs#1608)    )]
[1609](https://docs.rs#1609)    fn expect_throw(self, message: &str) -> T;
[1610](https://docs.rs#1610)}
[1611](https://docs.rs#1611)
[1612](https://docs.rs#1612)impl<T> UnwrapThrowExt<T> for Option<T> {
[1613](https://docs.rs#1613)    fn unwrap_throw(self) -> T {
[1614](https://docs.rs#1614)        const MSG: &str = "called `Option::unwrap_throw()` on a `None` value";
[1615](https://docs.rs#1615)
[1616](https://docs.rs#1616)        if cfg!(all(target_family = "wasm", not(target_os = "wasi"))) {
[1617](https://docs.rs#1617)            if let Some(val) = self {
[1618](https://docs.rs#1618)                val
[1619](https://docs.rs#1619)            } else if cfg!(debug_assertions) {
[1620](https://docs.rs#1620)                let loc = core::panic::Location::caller();
[1621](https://docs.rs#1621)                let msg = alloc::format!("{MSG} ({}:{}:{})", loc.file(), loc.line(), loc.column(),);
[1622](https://docs.rs#1622)
[1623](https://docs.rs#1623)                throw_str(&msg)
[1624](https://docs.rs#1624)            } else {
[1625](https://docs.rs#1625)                throw_str(MSG)
[1626](https://docs.rs#1626)            }
[1627](https://docs.rs#1627)        } else {
[1628](https://docs.rs#1628)            self.expect(MSG)
[1629](https://docs.rs#1629)        }
[1630](https://docs.rs#1630)    }
[1631](https://docs.rs#1631)
[1632](https://docs.rs#1632)    fn expect_throw(self, message: &str) -> T {
[1633](https://docs.rs#1633)        if cfg!(all(target_family = "wasm", not(target_os = "wasi"))) {
[1634](https://docs.rs#1634)            if let Some(val) = self {
[1635](https://docs.rs#1635)                val
[1636](https://docs.rs#1636)            } else if cfg!(debug_assertions) {
[1637](https://docs.rs#1637)                let loc = core::panic::Location::caller();
[1638](https://docs.rs#1638)                let msg =
[1639](https://docs.rs#1639)                    alloc::format!("{message} ({}:{}:{})", loc.file(), loc.line(), loc.column(),);
[1640](https://docs.rs#1640)
[1641](https://docs.rs#1641)                throw_str(&msg)
[1642](https://docs.rs#1642)            } else {
[1643](https://docs.rs#1643)                throw_str(message)
[1644](https://docs.rs#1644)            }
[1645](https://docs.rs#1645)        } else {
[1646](https://docs.rs#1646)            self.expect(message)
[1647](https://docs.rs#1647)        }
[1648](https://docs.rs#1648)    }
[1649](https://docs.rs#1649)}

[1655](https://docs.rs#1655)    fn unwrap_throw(self) -> T {
[1656](https://docs.rs#1656)        const MSG: &str = "called `Result::unwrap_throw()` on an `Err` value";
[1657](https://docs.rs#1657)

[1665](https://docs.rs#1665)                            "{MSG} ({}:{}:{}): {err:?}",

[1667](https://docs.rs#1667)                            loc.line(),

[1669](https://docs.rs#1669)                        );
[1670](https://docs.rs#1670)
[1671](https://docs.rs#1671)                        throw_str(&msg)
[1672](https://docs.rs#1672)                    } else {
[1673](https://docs.rs#1673)                        throw_str(MSG)
[1674](https://docs.rs#1674)                    }
[1675](https://docs.rs#1675)                }
[1676](https://docs.rs#1676)            }
[1677](https://docs.rs#1677)        } else {
[1678](https://docs.rs#1678)            self.expect(MSG)
[1679](https://docs.rs#1679)        }
[1680](https://docs.rs#1680)    }
[1681](https://docs.rs#1681)

[1741](https://docs.rs#1741)/// A wrapper type around slices and vectors for binding the `Uint8ClampedArray`

[1743](https://docs.rs#1743)///
[1744](https://docs.rs#1744)/// If you need to invoke a JS API which must take `Uint8ClampedArray` array,
[1745](https://docs.rs#1745)/// then you can define it as taking one of these types:
[1746](https://docs.rs#1746)///
[1747](https://docs.rs#1747)/// * `Clamped<&[u8]>`
[1748](https://docs.rs#1748)/// * `Clamped<&mut [u8]>`
[1749](https://docs.rs#1749)/// * `Clamped<Vec<u8>>`
[1750](https://docs.rs#1750)///
[1751](https://docs.rs#1751)/// All of these types will show up as `Uint8ClampedArray` in JS and will have
[1752](https://docs.rs#1752)/// different forms of ownership in Rust.
[1753](https://docs.rs#1753)#[derive(Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Debug, Eq)]
[1754](https://docs.rs#1754)pub struct Clamped<T>(pub T);
[1755](https://docs.rs#1755)
[1756](https://docs.rs#1756)impl<T> Deref for Clamped<T> {
[1757](https://docs.rs#1757)    type Target = T;
[1758](https://docs.rs#1758)
[1759](https://docs.rs#1759)    fn deref(&self) -> &T {
[1760](https://docs.rs#1760)        &self.0
[1761](https://docs.rs#1761)    }
[1762](https://docs.rs#1762)}
[1763](https://docs.rs#1763)
[1764](https://docs.rs#1764)impl<T> DerefMut for Clamped<T> {
[1765](https://docs.rs#1765)    fn deref_mut(&mut self) -> &mut T {
[1766](https://docs.rs#1766)        &mut self.0
[1767](https://docs.rs#1767)    }
[1768](https://docs.rs#1768)}
[1769](https://docs.rs#1769)
[1770](https://docs.rs#1770)/// Convenience type for use on exported `fn() -> Result<T, JsError>` functions, where you wish to
[1771](https://docs.rs#1771)/// throw a JavaScript `Error` object.
[1772](https://docs.rs#1772)///
[1773](https://docs.rs#1773)/// You can get wasm_bindgen to throw basic errors by simply returning
[1774](https://docs.rs#1774)/// `Err(JsError::new("message"))` from such a function.
[1775](https://docs.rs#1775)///
[1776](https://docs.rs#1776)/// For more complex error handling, `JsError` implements `From<T> where T: std::error::Error` by
[1777](https://docs.rs#1777)/// converting it to a string, so you can use it with `?`. Many Rust error types already do this,
[1778](https://docs.rs#1778)/// and you can use [`thiserror`](https://crates.io/crates/thiserror) to derive Display
[1779](https://docs.rs#1779)/// implementations easily or use any number of boxed error types that implement it already.
[1780](https://docs.rs#1780)///
[1781](https://docs.rs#1781)///
[1782](https://docs.rs#1782)/// To allow JavaScript code to catch only your errors, you may wish to add a subclass of `Error`
[1783](https://docs.rs#1783)/// in a JS module, and then implement `Into<JsValue>` directly on a type and instantiate that
[1784](https://docs.rs#1784)/// subclass. In that case, you would not need `JsError` at all.
[1785](https://docs.rs#1785)///
[1786](https://docs.rs#1786)/// ### Basic example
[1787](https://docs.rs#1787)///
[1788](https://docs.rs#1788)/// ```rust,no_run
[1789](https://docs.rs#1789)/// use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
[1790](https://docs.rs#1790)///
[1791](https://docs.rs#1791)/// #[wasm_bindgen]
[1792](https://docs.rs#1792)/// pub fn throwing_function() -> Result<(), JsError> {
[1793](https://docs.rs#1793)///     Err(JsError::new("message"))
[1794](https://docs.rs#1794)/// }
[1795](https://docs.rs#1795)/// ```
[1796](https://docs.rs#1796)///
[1797](https://docs.rs#1797)/// ### Complex Example
[1798](https://docs.rs#1798)///
[1799](https://docs.rs#1799)/// ```rust,no_run
[1800](https://docs.rs#1800)/// use wasm_bindgen::prelude::*;
[1801](https://docs.rs#1801)///
[1802](https://docs.rs#1802)/// #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
[1803](https://docs.rs#1803)/// enum MyErrorType {
[1804](https://docs.rs#1804)///     SomeError,
[1805](https://docs.rs#1805)/// }
[1806](https://docs.rs#1806)///
[1807](https://docs.rs#1807)/// use core::fmt;
[1808](https://docs.rs#1808)/// impl std::error::Error for MyErrorType {}
[1809](https://docs.rs#1809)/// impl fmt::Display for MyErrorType {
[1810](https://docs.rs#1810)///     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[1811](https://docs.rs#1811)///         write!(f, "display implementation becomes the error message")
[1812](https://docs.rs#1812)///     }
[1813](https://docs.rs#1813)/// }
[1814](https://docs.rs#1814)///
[1815](https://docs.rs#1815)/// fn internal_api() -> Result<(), MyErrorType> {
[1816](https://docs.rs#1816)///     Err(MyErrorType::SomeError)
[1817](https://docs.rs#1817)/// }
[1818](https://docs.rs#1818)///
[1819](https://docs.rs#1819)/// #[wasm_bindgen]
[1820](https://docs.rs#1820)/// pub fn throwing_function() -> Result<(), JsError> {
[1821](https://docs.rs#1821)///     internal_api()?;
[1822](https://docs.rs#1822)///     Ok(())
[1823](https://docs.rs#1823)/// }
[1824](https://docs.rs#1824)///
[1825](https://docs.rs#1825)/// ```
[1826](https://docs.rs#1826)#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
[1827](https://docs.rs#1827)#[repr(transparent)]
[1828](https://docs.rs#1828)pub struct JsError {
[1829](https://docs.rs#1829)    value: JsValue,
[1830](https://docs.rs#1830)}
[1831](https://docs.rs#1831)
[1832](https://docs.rs#1832)impl JsError {

# IntoJsGeneric in wasm_bindgen::convert - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-bindgen/0.2.126/wasm_bindgen/convert/trait.IntoJsGeneric.html

```
pub trait IntoJsGeneric {
    type
```
[JsCanon](https://docs.rs#associatedtype.JsCanon): [JsGeneric](https://docs.rs/trait.JsGeneric.html);
    // Required method
    fn [to_js](https://docs.rs#tymethod.to_js)(self) -> Self::[JsCanon](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoJsGeneric.html#associatedtype.JsCanon);
}## Expand description

Value conversion from a type into its canonical [ JsGeneric](https://docs.rs/trait.JsGeneric.html) form.

This trait allows types to be converted into JsGeneric supported types, which are required to be erasably generic with JsValue.

The single associated type — rather than a free type parameter bounded by
`AsRef<T>` — is what makes collection-style APIs infer annotation-free.
Given an input `A`, there is exactly one `A::JsCanon`, so rustc never has
to search across multiple `AsRef` impls to pick a target element type.

[§](https://docs.rs#implementations-1)Implementations

Provided impls:

- `JsValue`
- Every `#[wasm_bindgen]`-imported type (identity — emitted by the macro).
- Every generic `js_sys`container (`Array<T>`,`Promise<T>`,`Set<T>`, …) provides its own identity impl owned by`js_sys`.
- References to cloneable implementors, so borrowed iteration can still produce owned JS-generic values.

This trait is deliberately *not* blanket-implemented over all [ JsGeneric](https://docs.rs/trait.JsGeneric.html)
types: each implementor explicitly opts in, which leaves room for future
wrapper types to pick a non-identity

[.](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoJsGeneric.html#associatedtype.JsCanon)

`Self::JsCanon`[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

## Required Associated Types[§](https://docs.rs#required-associated-types)

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# JsGeneric in wasm_bindgen::convert - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/wasm-bindgen/0.2.126/wasm_bindgen/convert/trait.JsGeneric.html

```
pub trait JsGeneric:

```
[ErasableGeneric](https://docs.rs/trait.ErasableGeneric.html)<Repr = [JsValue](https://docs.rs/struct.JsValue.html)>
    + [UpcastFrom](https://docs.rs/trait.UpcastFrom.html)<Self>
    + [Upcast](https://docs.rs/trait.Upcast.html)<Self>
    + [Upcast](https://docs.rs/trait.Upcast.html)<[JsValue](https://docs.rs/struct.JsValue.html)>
    + [JsCast](https://docs.rs/trait.JsCast.html)
    + 'static { }## Expand description

A convenience trait for types that erase to [ JsValue](https://docs.rs/struct.JsValue.html).

This is a shorthand for `ErasableGeneric<Repr = JsValue>`, used as a bound
on generic parameters that must be representable as JavaScript values.

[§](https://docs.rs#when-to-use)When to Use

Use `JsGeneric` as a trait bound when you need a generic type that:

- Can be passed to/from JavaScript
- Is type-erased to `JsValue`at the FFI boundary

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use wasm_bindgen::JsGeneric;
fn process_js_values<T: JsGeneric>(items: &[T]) {
    // T can be any JS-compatible type
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#implementors-1)Implementors

This trait is automatically implemented for all types that implement
`ErasableGeneric<Repr = JsValue>`, including:

- All `js_sys`types (`Object`,`Array`,`Function`, etc.)
- `JsValue`itself
- Custom types imported via `#[wasm_bindgen]`
